chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Isa from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: 'Does a man perform Tawaf on behalf of another man while both are residing in Mecca?' He said: 'No, but he performs Tawaf on behalf of a man who is absent from Mecca.' I said: 'And what is the measure of that absence?' He said: 'Ten miles.'

And whoever commits a minor or major impurity outside the Sanctuary and seeks refuge in the Sanctuary, then restriction is placed upon him regarding food and drink until he goes out and the hadd punishment is carried out upon him. And if he commits impurity within the Sanctuary, then the hadd punishment is carried out upon him within it. Narrated.

key_terms.يُقَامَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَدُّ: the hadd punishment is carried out upon him

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for performing Tawaf on behalf of someone else and the ruling for escaping punishment by entering the Haram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s distinction between Tawaf for the absent (where the representative must be in Mecca while the principal is away by at least ten miles) versus the absent performing it themselves. The hadith further clarifies the legal mechanism of 'Iqlal' (restriction of sustenance) for those seeking refuge in the Haram to evade punishment for crimes committed outside its boundaries, a unique jurisprudential concept in Shia fiqh.
